implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) was approved 2026-09-04. Device cloud access procedures (production access requests, tenant administrator setup) are due 2026-11-30.

Workforce accounts come from HR onboarding tickets through the identity provider. Clinician accounts are managed by each hospital's administrator through federation or local portal accounts. Gap: 14 support and DevOps engineers hold standing production roles covering all tenants, and no quarterly access review is performed.
evidence: IdP group export; production role list

implementation_statement: Every portal and API request carries a tenant ID that the application checks, and the database enforces row-level security by tenant. Portal roles: clinician, charge nurse, hospital administrator, company support (read-only by default).
evidence: Role matrix; row-level security policy; code review records

implementation_statement: Service-to-service traffic is limited by container network policies. HL7 results leave only to registered hospital endpoints. Gap: the processing services have unrestricted outbound internet access.
Code changes need a second reviewer. Gap: the same administrators manage production and backups, so one compromised account could delete both.
Engineers have read-only access to non-production by default. Gap: standing all-tenant production access for 14 engineers (see AC-2); just-in-time access planned for 2026-11-30.
The identity provider locks workforce accounts after 10 failed attempts. Portal local accounts lock for 15 minutes after 5 failed attempts.
Support and DevOps laptops lock after 10 minutes idle through device management.
Portal sessions end after 15 minutes idle and after 12 hours in total.
Administrative access to the cloud console and to production containers goes through the identity provider with MFA and a managed bastion service. No direct internet administration ports are open.
All workforce members complete annual security awareness training, including HIPAA basics for staff who support the device cloud.
Planned: annual secure development and HIPAA training for cloud engineers and support staff with production access, starting 2027-01.

The cloud control plane, the identity provider, and the portal log sign-ins, administrative actions, and data exports. Gap: database queries by support engineers are not logged at statement level, so bulk reads cannot be detected.
Portal and API audit records include user, tenant, patient record ID, action, timestamp, and source address.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: no one reviews device cloud audit logs. Planned: weekly review of privileged activity and alerting on bulk exports and cross-tenant errors, starting 2026-11.
The cloud audit trail is write-protected by the provider. Gap: application logs in the log analytics service can be deleted by any of 9 administrators.
Gap: application and audit logs are kept 30 days. Planned: 1-year retention for audit events and 6-year retention for security documentation (POL-01).
Audit record generation for the control plane is on by default and cannot be disabled by tenant users.
The device cloud has a SOC 2 Type 1 report (Security) as of 2026-03-31. An internal control assessment was performed 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-14 (P07).

Each hospital interface is covered by the BAA and an interface specification. Gap: the 12 site-to-site VPN connections for HL7 have no interconnection security terms (contacts, change notice, incident notice).
Weaknesses are tracked in the P07 POA&M with owners and dates.
Planned: monthly security metrics (patch age, open vulnerabilities, access review status) reported to the COO from 2026-12.

implementation_statement: Gap: the device cloud has never had an independent penetration test. First test, including cross-tenant cases, is contracted for 2026-11.

implementation_statement: All cloud infrastructure is defined as code in the repository. Container base images are built from a hardened internal image.
Changes go through pull requests with a second reviewer and automated tests. Gap: emergency console changes are not recorded or reviewed after the fact.
Container and database settings follow the internal hardening standard. Gap: the standard has no documented deviations process, and 3 legacy services run as root.
Only required ports are exposed: device ingestion (mutual TLS), portal (HTTPS), and HL7 over VPN.

Infrastructure components are inventoried from infrastructure code. Gap: there is no SBOM for device cloud software, so affected services cannot be found quickly when a component vulnerability is announced.
A contingency planning policy and procedures are due 2026-12-31.
A draft device cloud recovery runbook exists. The BIA (P05) set an RTO of 2 hours and an RPO of 15 minutes for remote monitoring. Gap: the plan is not approved and does not cover a regional outage.
Gap: no restore or failover test has been performed. The first restore test is scheduled for 2026-10-20.
The managed database takes daily backups with point-in-time recovery (5-minute log interval), copied to a second region. Gap: backups are not immutable and share administrators with production.
Services can be redeployed from infrastructure code. Gap: database recovery steps are untested.
All workforce users authenticate with unique accounts through the identity provider. No shared accounts exist in the device cloud.
MFA with phishing-resistant hardware keys is required for all privileged cloud and production roles.
MFA is required for all non-privileged workforce access to the portal support views and SaaS tools.

PM-2 monitors authenticate with unique device certificates (mutual TLS) issued by the device cloud's private certificate authority. Gap: PM-1 monitors authenticate with one shared API key per hospital.
Service secrets are stored in the cloud secrets manager and rotated every 90 days. Gap: PM-1 per-hospital API keys have never been rotated.
Clinicians sign in through their hospital's identity provider (28 hospitals) or through local portal accounts with MFA (12 hospitals).
POL-03 Incident Response Policy, covering product security incidents, was approved 2026-09-04 (P06).
The P08 runbook for an exploited fielded-device vulnerability was approved 2026-09-04. Gap: it has not been exercised; the first tabletop is due 2026-11-30.
Business associate notice duties to hospitals (164.410) and FDA reporting decision points are in the P08 notification matrix. Gap: BAA-specific notice terms are not yet in one register.
POL-03 and the P08 runbook form the plan. Gap: a ransomware runbook for the device cloud is not yet written.
Physical access to data centers is controlled by the cloud provider.
This SSP.
POL-05 Acceptable Use was approved 2026-09-04. Acknowledgments are due 2026-10-31.

implementation_statement: Risk tolerance and acceptance authority are set in POL-01 and applied in the P01 register.
Background checks are completed before hire for all staff.
Accounts are disabled in the identity provider the same business day as termination.
The device cloud is categorized Moderate (section 6 of this SSP).
Risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01).
Monthly authenticated scans of cloud workloads; dependency and container scanning on every build. Gap: no dynamic testing of the portal and no remediation time limits.
Gap: no public vulnerability disclosure policy or reporting channel commitment. A CVD policy covering devices and the device cloud is due 2026-10-31.
Security and BAA terms are in the cloud provider and ticketing contracts. Gap: no standard security terms for new SaaS vendors.
Device software follows the QMS design controls with security requirements. Gap: the device cloud has no documented secure development framework or complete threat model.
Subcontractor BAAs are in place with the cloud provider and the ticketing vendor. Gap: the log analytics service receives PHI without a BAA.
Static analysis, unit tests, and dependency scanning run on every build. Gap: no dynamic testing, fuzzing of the ingestion API, or independent testing (see CA-8).
regulatory_driver: N31-33-R05 (524B(b)(2)); FDA premarket guidance (2026-02-03) section V.C

implementation_statement: Provider denial-of-service protection and autoscaling front the ingestion and portal endpoints.
A web application firewall fronts the portal. Databases and services sit in private subnets. HL7 traffic uses site-to-site VPNs.
TLS 1.2 or higher on all external interfaces; mutual TLS for PM-2 devices; IPsec VPNs for HL7.

Data keys and the device certificate authority keys are held in the cloud key management service with non-exportable keys. The firmware code-signing key is outside this boundary (SYS-04, see section 8).
Encryption uses the provider's validated cryptographic modules as stated in its SOC 2 system description.
Portal sessions use secure, HTTP-only cookies bound to the session; device sessions are bound to the device certificate.
The database, object storage, and backups are encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys.
Container images are rebuilt weekly with current patches. Gap: no written remediation time limits by severity.
EDR runs on all support and DevOps endpoints. Uploaded files in the portal (reports) are scanned before storage.
Gap: no security monitoring or alerting for the device cloud. Planned: alerting on privileged activity, bulk exports, and anomalous device traffic by 2027-01.
The Product Security Lead reads supplier and CISA advisories. Gap: no defined sources, frequency, or record.
The update service distributes only PM-2 firmware signed in the build pipeline, and devices verify the signature. Gap: device cloud container images are not signed or verified at deployment.
The ingestion API validates message schema, size, and value ranges and rejects malformed messages.
Patient data is deleted after the 24-month BAA retention period by an automated job. Gap: PHI in application logs is copied to the log analytics service.
A supply chain risk management plan covering software components and SaaS vendors is due 2027-03-31.
Dependency scanning covers cloud code. Gap: no approved-component list or dependency pinning policy for firmware builds.
